aspect: EXAMPLE - the Apple Store, Georgia, June 2012
description: Sahar Sabet, 19 and a US citizen, was refused an iPad at an Apple store in Georgia after an employee overheard her speaking Farsi with her uncle. She was told: 'I just can't sell this to you. Our countries have such bad relations.' She already owned an iPhone and a MacBook. She called it 'very hurtful, very embarrassing' and walked out in tears.
energy_note: Refused for the language you were speaking to your uncle.

description: When Sabet returned with a WSB-TV crew the same employee refused again, and the manager produced the sales policy stating Apple products must not be sold for export to Iran, North Korea or other embargoed countries.
energy_note: Policy read aloud to justify it.

aspect: EXAMPLE - a second customer, a second store
description: Zack Jafarzadeh had the same experience at a different Apple store.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the employee was Iranian himself
description: The staff member recognised Farsi because he was from Iran. The enforcement ran through someone from the same community.

aspect: There was no law requiring it
description: A State Department representative clarified there was no policy or law prohibiting Apple from selling in the US to anyone intending to use the goods in the US, including customers of Iranian descent or citizenship. A licence is needed only to take high-technology goods TO Iran.
energy_note: The refusal was not required by anything.

description: OFAC rules make a person liable for exporting goods they know or have reason to know are intended for Iran - which pushes the judgement down to the sales associate, who has civil and criminal exposure and no training. Overcaution is the rational individual response.
energy_note: The system delegates the discrimination to a 22-year-old on a till.

description: Sabet later received an apology from Apple customer relations and was told she could buy the iPad online. CAIR called on Apple to change the policy; NIAC's Jamal Abdi attacked the practice in a New York Times op-ed.

Omid goes to buy a laptop. The assistant asks where he is from, then asks a manager, then comes back and says the system needs an address verification they cannot complete today. He buys the same laptop online that evening, delivered to the same address.
energy_note: Refused in person, sold to online, by the same company.
